options.text: In times of national crisis, citizens tend to cleave to traditional values and established social structures.

options.text: The chef used a heavy iron utensil to quickly cleave the dense bone of the carcass during preparation.

options.text: Engineers designed the supersonic aircraft hull to smoothly cleave through dense atmospheric resistance.
options.html: Engineers designed the supersonic aircraft hull to smoothly cleave through dense atmospheric resistance.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. In times of national crisis, citizens tend to cleave to traditional values and established social structures..

Key Points

  • The word "cleave" is a homonym, meaning it has two different meanings depending on the context.
  • One meaning of "cleave" is to stick closely, remain faithful, or adhere to something. (हिंदी में: चिपके रहना, वफादार रहना)
    • Example: During tough times, she would cleave to her faith for strength.
  • In the context of the correct option, "cleave" is used to mean adhering or remaining faithful, as citizens are said to stick to traditional values during crises.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. In times of national crisis, citizens tend to cleave to traditional values and established social structures.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 2: The chef used a heavy iron utensil to quickly cleave the dense bone of the carcass during preparation.
    • Here, "cleave" means to split or cut something apart, typically with force. (हिंदी में: काटना या फाड़ना)
    • Example: He used an axe to cleave the wood into smaller pieces.
    • Since this meaning does not align with the context of adhering or sticking closely, this is not the correct answer.
  • Option 3: The extreme geological pressure caused the diamond specimen to cleave perfectly along its natural crystalline plane.
    • Here, "cleave" again means to split or divide, specifically referring to a natural division in the diamond. (हिंदी में: विभाजित होना)
    • Example: The jeweler examined how the gemstone would cleave under pressure.
    • This does not match the intended meaning of "to stick closely," so it is incorrect.
  • Option 4: Engineers designed the supersonic aircraft hull to smoothly cleave through dense atmospheric resistance.
    • In this context, "cleave" refers to cutting or moving through something smoothly, such as air or water. (हिंदी में: चीर कर आगे बढ़ना)
    • Example: The boat cleaved through the water with ease.
    • Again, this meaning does not correspond to the correct context of sticking or adhering, so this option is not correct.

questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, sentences of a paragraph have been jumbled and labelled as A, B, C, and D. You are required to rearrange the jumbled sentences of the paragraph and mark your response accordingly by selecting the correct option.

A: Various governments have made efforts since the 1970s to reduce the release of sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxide into the atmosphere with positive results.

B: Acid rain is caused by emissions of sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxide, which react with the water molecules in the atmosphere to produce acids.

C: It can have harmful effects on plants, aquatic animals, and infrastructure.

D: Acid rain is a rain or any other form of precipitation that is unusually acidic, meaning that it has elevated levels of hydrogen ions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. DCBA.

  • D is the first sentence because it introduces the subject of the passage 'acid rain' and explains it.
  • Both B and C can be placed in the second position, but since BA would form a pair, C would follow D.
  • B talks of 'emissions of sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxide' and A talks of governments' efforts to reduce the release of sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxide into the atmosphere. Therefore, A must follow B.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. "Had you followed my instructions, the experiment would not have failed so miserably." .

Key Points

  • The given sentence is an example of the third conditional, which is used to describe unreal past situations and their imagined outcomes.
  • The structure of the third conditional is "If + past perfect, would have + past participle".
  • The sentence in direct speech uses "Had you followed" to indicate the past perfect tense and "would not have failed" to express the hypothetical result in the past.

Correct sentence: The teacher said to the students, "Had you followed my instructions, the experiment would not have failed so miserably."

Additional Information

  • 1st Conditional Sentence:
    • Structure: If + Present Simple, will + base verb.
    • Example: If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.
    • Usage: Describes real or possible situations in the future with likely outcomes.
  • 2nd Conditional Sentence:
    • Structure: If + Past Simple, would + base verb.
    • Example: If I were rich, I would travel the world.
    • Usage: Refers to unreal or hypothetical situations in the present or future.
  • 3rd Conditional Sentence:
    • Structure: If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.
    • Example: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
    • Usage: Refers to unreal past situations and their imagined outcomes.

(1) The uncataloged ledger containing detailed logs of the colonial trading company’s / (2) illicit maritime transactions had laid undisturbed in the damp basement / (3) of the provincial archives building for over a century / (4) before it was discovered during a routine structural inspection.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. had lain .

Key Points

  • The error lies in part (2) of the sentence: "had laid."
  • The verb "lay" (past tense: "laid") is a transitive verb, meaning it requires an object. For example, "She laid the book on the table."
  • In this context, the verb "lie" (past tense: "lay," past participle: "lain") is the correct choice as it is an intransitive verb, used to describe the state of resting or being in a horizontal position. Example: "The book had lain on the table."
  • Since the sentence refers to the ledger "resting undisturbed," the correct form is "had lain."

Correct sentence: The uncataloged ledger containing detailed logs of the colonial trading company’s illicit maritime transactions had lain undisturbed in the damp basement of the provincial archives building for over a century before it was discovered during a routine structural inspection.

Additional Information

  • Usage of "Lay" and "Lie":
    • Lay: Transitive verb, requires an object. Example: "I lay the plates on the table."
    • Lie: Intransitive verb, does not require an object. Example: "I lie down to rest."
    • Conjugation of "Lay": lay, laid, laid (e.g., "I laid the book on the table.")
    • Conjugation of "Lie": lie, lay, lain (e.g., "The book had lain on the table.")

The correct answer is 'He cleared a space on his bed for his sister to take a seat and flopped down in his swivel chair.'

Key Points 

  • The given blank needs the correct word to form the correct collocation phrase.
  • Based on the given options the correct phrase for the given blank is 'take a seat'.
  • "Take a seat" means to sit down.
  • Thus, option 4 is the correct answer as it is the only sentence containing the correct phrase. 
     

Correct sentence - He cleared a space on his bed for his sister to take a seat and flopped down in his swivel chair.

Additional Information 

  • A collocation is two or more words that often go together.
  • These combinations just sound "right" to native English speakers, who use them all the time. On the other hand, other combinations may be unnatural and just sound "wrong".
    • Example - fast food is a collocation. It is incorrect to say quick food, although quick is a synonym of fast. 
  • There are several different types of collocation made from combinations of verb, noun, adjective etc. Some of the most common types are:
    • adverb + adjective: completely satisfied (NOT downright satisfied)
    • adjective + noun: excruciating pain (NOT excruciating joy)
    • noun + noun: a surge of anger (NOT a rush of anger)
    • noun + verb: lions roar (NOT lions shout)
    • verb + noun: commit suicide (NOT undertake suicide)
    • verb + expression with preposition: burst into tears (NOT blow up in tears)
    • verb + adverb: wave frantically (NOT wave feverishly)

Key Points
  • The passage discusses the paradox of technological progress, noting that while it improves efficiency, it also creates significant ethical and societal challenges.
  • It highlights examples such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Social Media to illustrate how benefits like automation and connectivity come with risks like employment displacement, misinformation, and privacy erosion.
  • The author argues that innovation is not a straightforward path to utopia but requires critical scrutiny and ethical governance to address issues like algorithmic opacity and the global digital divide.
  • Therefore, the statement that technology offers benefits while introducing complex challenges that require examination best encapsulates the central thesis of the text.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Summary: 'While technology offers numerous benefits, it also introduces complex ethical and societal challenges that must be critically examined.'
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1 is too narrow; social media is mentioned only as one of several examples to support the broader argument about technology.
  • Option 2 is incorrect because the passage explicitly states that the pursuit of innovation engenders complexities and challenges ethical frameworks, rather than eliminating them.
  • Option 4 is inaccurate as the author characterizes technological progress as 'fraught with dilemmas' and 'dual-edged,' acknowledging significant potential drawbacks and inequalities.

Therefore, the correct answer is Introduction of a paradox with supporting examples leading to a call for critical evaluation.

questions.question: Which of the following is the closest synonym for the word "obfuscated" as it is used in the second paragraph ("...can be obfuscated as a naturally occurring zoonotic spillover...")?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the closest synonym for the word "obfuscated" as it is used in the second paragraph ("...can be obfuscated as a naturally occurring zoonotic spillover...")?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2'.
 
Key Points
  • Option 1: Clarified
    • This is incorrect. "Clarified" means made clear or easier to understand, whereas "obfuscated" means made obscure, hidden, or difficult to recognize.
  • Option 2: Camouflaged
    • This is correct. In the passage, "obfuscated" means disguised, concealed, or hidden so that a biological attack appears to be a naturally occurring zoonotic spillover. "Camouflaged" is the closest synonym in this context.
  • Option 3: Amplified
    • This is incorrect. "Amplified" means increased or intensified, which is unrelated to the idea of concealing or disguising something.
  • Option 4: Eradicated
    • This is incorrect. "Eradicated" means completely destroyed or eliminated, which does not match the meaning of "obfuscated."
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2: Camouflaged.
 
Additional Information
  • Obfuscated means made obscure, hidden, disguised, or deliberately difficult to understand.
  • Camouflaged is the closest synonym because both words convey the idea of concealing the true nature or origin of something.
  • Clarified is an antonym, while Amplified and Eradicated have entirely different meanings.

Key Points

  • Venus is often referred to as Earth's "sister planet" because of its similar size, composition, and proximity to the Sun.
  • The greenhouse effect is a natural process that warms the Planet’s surface.
  • Venus has a thick atmosphere composed mainly of carbon dioxide (about 96.5%) and nitrogen, with clouds of sulfuric acid.
  • However, the thick cloud cover and high concentration of greenhouse gases trap the heat, preventing it from escaping back into space.
  • This process leads to extremely high surface temperatures on Venus, averaging around 465 degrees Celsius.
  • The atmospheric pressure on Venus is about 92 times that of Earth’s at sea level.

Additional Information

  • Venus has a high albedo due to its thick cloud cover, reflecting about 70% of incoming sunlight.
  • Tidal heating is a phenomenon that occurs when a celestial body experiences internal heating due to the gravitational forces exerted by nearby objects.
  • The amount of tidal heating depends on several factors, including the mass of the two interacting bodies, their distance from each other, and the orbital eccentricity.
  • Gravitational compression occurs when the weight of the material within a celestial body causes it to collapse under its own gravity.
  • The gravitational force is so strong that not even light can escape from within the event horizon.
  • The solar wind is primarily composed of charged particles, including protons (about 95%), electrons (about 4%), and alpha particles (helium nuclei, about 1%). 
  • On Earth, solar wind absorption is responsible for creating auroras (the Northern and Southern Lights).

Key Points

    • The Civil Disobedience Movement (1930) saw less Muslim participation compared to the Non-Cooperation Movement.
    • One significant reason was the Congress's failure to adequately address specific Muslim concerns.
    • There was an absence of a robust alliance with major Muslim political groups during the Civil Disobedience Movement.

Additional Information

 

The Civil Disobedience Movement in India, initiated by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930, had several important features:

  • Non-Violent Resistance: Emphasis on non-violent methods to resist British laws and policies. This included peaceful protests, non-cooperation, and passive resistance.
  • Salt March: The movement began with the Salt March (Dandi March) where Gandhi walked over 240 miles to the Arabian Sea to produce salt, symbolizing defiance of British monopoly and taxation on salt.
  • Boycott of British Goods: Widespread boycott of British imported goods, legal institutions, schools, and colleges. People were encouraged to use Indian-made goods and promote khadi (hand-spun cloth).
  • Mass Participation: The movement saw the participation of a large number of Indians from various strata of society, including farmers, laborers, students, and women.
  • Civil Disobedience: Deliberate and public refusal to obey certain laws, demands, and commands of the British government. This included non-payment of taxes, illegal production of salt, and refusal to follow British rules.
  • Spread Across the Country: Unlike previous movements, the Civil Disobedience Movement spread to both urban and rural areas, making it widespread across India.
  • Repressive Measures by the British: The British responded with repressive measures. Thousands of participants were arrested, including Gandhi and other prominent leaders. There were crackdowns on satyagrahis (non-violent protestors) and imposition of martial law in some regions.
  • Women’s Involvement: Significant involvement of women, who participated in protests, picketing, and leading marches. Figures like Sarojini Naidu played crucial roles.
  • Economic Impact: The boycott of British goods and encouragement of Indian industries led to economic impacts on both British businesses and local economies.
  • Negotiations and Dialogues: It prompted negotiations between the Indian National Congress and the British government, such as the Gandhi-Irwin Pact in 1931, which temporarily halted the movement and led to Gandhi attending the Round Table Conference in London.
  • Strengthening of Nationalism: The movement significantly strengthened the sense of nationalism and unity among Indians against British colonial rule.

    • Further influence of atmospheric pressure and insolation causes variation in winds movements which affects ocean currents eventually.
  • Rotation of Earth
    • The Coriolis effect is a result of the rotation of the earth. 
    • Coriolis force causes the matter to move right in the northern hemisphere and left in the southern hemisphere.

questions.question: Who was the President of India at the time of proclamation of emergency in 1975?
questions.questionHtml: Who was the President of India at the time of proclamation of emergency in 1975?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed.

Key Points

  • Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed was the fifth President of India, serving from 1974 until his death in 1977.
  • He was in office when Prime Minister Indira Gandhi declared a state of emergency on 25 June 1975.
  • During his tenure, the Emergency lasted for 21 months, during which civil liberties were suspended and the press was censored.
  • Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed was a key figure during the Emergency period, often endorsing the government's controversial actions.

Additional Information

  • State of Emergency in India (1975-1977)
    • The Emergency was declared by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on the grounds of internal disturbances.
    • It was a period marked by significant political changes, including the suspension of elections and civil liberties.
    • During this period, political opponents were arrested, and press censorship was enforced rigorously.
    • The Emergency is often cited as one of the most controversial periods in the history of independent India.
  • Role of the President during the Emergency
    • As the head of state, the President of India has the power to declare a state of emergency under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution.
    • Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed played a crucial role by endorsing the Emergency declaration, which was a decision taken by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
    • The President's role during this period was largely seen as a formality, as the real power was exercised by the Prime Minister and her advisors.
    • The Emergency period raised questions about the extent of the President's powers and the checks and balances in the Indian political system.
  • Impact of the Emergency
    • The Emergency had a profound impact on Indian democracy, leading to widespread human rights violations and political repression.
    • It led to the birth of several new political movements and parties, including the Janata Party, which eventually came to power in 1977.
    • The period also saw significant amendments to the Indian Constitution, some of which were later repealed to restore democratic norms.
    • The legacy of the Emergency continues to influence Indian politics, serving as a cautionary tale about the misuse of executive power.

questions.question: Which river originates south of the equator and flows north through north-eastern Africa to drain into the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.questionHtml: Which river originates south of the equator and flows north through north-eastern Africa to drain into the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.solution: The Nile River originates from Lake Victoria in East Africa and flows northward through northeastern Africa, draining into the Mediterranean Sea. It is approximately 6,650 kilometers long, making it one of the world's longest rivers. The Nile is crucial for agriculture in Egypt and Sudan and was historically significant to ancient civilizations. The river has two primary sources: Lake Victoria and the Blue Nile from Lake Tana in Ethiopia. It flows through Uganda, Sudan, and Egypt, eventually forming the Nile Delta before emptying into the Mediterranean. The Nile's length has been contested by the Amazon River in recent studies.
